title: GOD WILL SURELY COME TO YOUR AID

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Joseph said to his brothers, 'I am about to die. But God will surely come to your aid and take you up out of this land to the land he promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.'" — Gen 50:24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph's dying words are not about himself. They are about what God will do after he is gone.

"God will surely come to your aid." He is certain. He will not live to see it, and there is nothing in the present circumstances to suggest it — the family is comfortable in Egypt, well established, with no reason to leave. But God had made a promise to Abraham, and Joseph believes it absolutely.

That confidence would be needed. Four hundred years later, when Israel groaned under slavery, this word would still be there. God had said He would come. And He did.

Hebrews singles out this exact moment as Joseph's great act of faith: "By faith Joseph, when his end was near, spoke about the exodus of the Israelites from Egypt" (Heb 11:22). Not his rise to power. Not his forgiveness. This — believing a promise he would never see fulfilled.

Faith is not certainty about our circumstances. It is certainty about God's character. He keeps His word, whether or not we are there to watch.

What Joseph believed in outline, we have seen fulfilled in full: God came to our aid Himself, in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What promise of God do you need to hold onto, even without seeing it?
2. What do you want your last words to point people towards?
3. How does God's track record of keeping promises strengthen you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You keep Your word across generations. Give me faith like Joseph's — certain about Your character even when I cannot see the outcome. Amen.
